title: Car Knocking Over Humps: Causes | SG Car Workshop
h1: Car knocking or clunking over speed humps
desc: Why a car knocks, clunks or rattles over humps and bumps, what to tell the workshop, and workshops customers mention for suspension and noise work.
lede: A knock or clunk from underneath when you go over a speed hump is usually a worn suspension part. Most causes are common and fixable, but the exact part has to be found by looking at the car on a lift.
causes: These small linkages connect the anti-roll bar to the suspension. When they wear, they clunk over uneven roads and bumps, often at low speed.
Worn shock absorbers or top mounts
A shock absorber that is tired or leaking oil can knock or let the car bounce more than it should. The mounts at the top can also wear and knock.
Worn arm bushes or ball joints
Rubber bushes in the control arms and the ball joints wear with age and mileage. They can knock over bumps and may also make the steering feel loose.
A loose heat shield, a worn exhaust hanger or an under-car cover that has come loose can rattle over bumps. These are usually quick to check.
Wear at the drive shaft joints
Worn joints more often click when turning, but a worn joint can also knock when the car moves up and down.
tell: Where it comes from: front or rear, left or right.
When it happens: only over humps, when turning, when braking, or on every bump.
The sound: a single clunk, a rattle or a creak.
How long it has been going on and whether it is getting louder.
Any recent work on the suspension, tyres or exhaust.
Ask for an under-car inspection on a lift.
urgent: If the steering feels loose, the car pulls to one side, you see fluid leaking from a shock absorber, or a loud knock suddenly gets worse, have it checked before driving further.
faqs: Is a knock over humps dangerous?
It can be a small thing, such as a loose cover, or a worn part that affects how the car handles. Because you cannot tell which from the sound alone, it is worth having it inspected soon.
Can I find the noise myself?
You can note where and when it happens, which helps the workshop a lot. Finding the exact part usually needs the car lifted and the suspension checked by hand.

title: Car Aircon Not Cold: Causes | SG Car Workshop
h1: Car aircon not cold
desc: Why a car aircon blows warm or weak air, what to tell the workshop, and workshops customers mention for aircon servicing and repair.
lede: When the aircon is not as cold as it used to be, the cause is usually one of a handful of common faults. Some are simple, some need parts, and a gas top-up alone only helps if nothing is leaking.
causes: Aircon gas does not get used up. If the level is low, there is a leak somewhere, often a hose joint, the condenser or a seal. Topping up without finding the leak means the cold fades again.
The condenser sits at the front of the car like a small radiator. If it is clogged with dirt or damaged, the system cannot shed heat and cools poorly, especially in traffic.
The compressor drives the system. If it does not engage, or is worn, the air stays warm. You may hear a change in noise when the aircon switches on.
Weak airflow from a dirty cabin filter or blower
If cold air comes out but only weakly, a clogged cabin filter or a weak blower motor is a common reason.
A fan that does not run, a faulty pressure switch, a relay or a fuse can stop the system from working properly, often only when the car is standing still.
tell: Is the air warm, only cool, or cold but weak?
Does it get worse in traffic or when idling?
Do you hear the compressor switch on, or any unusual noise or smell?
When was the aircon last serviced?
Ask whether they will check for leaks, not only top up the gas.
urgent: A burning smell, a loud grinding from the compressor, or a belt noise needs checking soon, as a failing compressor can damage the drive belt.
faqs: Why does my aircon get cold only when driving?
This can point to the condenser fan or airflow over the condenser. At speed, air passes through naturally; when standing, the fan has to do the work.
Is an aircon flush the same as a gas top-up?
No. A flush cleans the system and a top-up adds gas. Which one you need depends on what the workshop finds, so ask them to explain.

title: Car Won't Start: Battery and Starter | SG Car Workshop
h1: Car won't start: battery, starter or something else?
desc: What the sounds mean when a car won't start, likely causes, what to tell the workshop, and workshops customers mention for starter and breakdown work.
lede: What you hear when you turn the key or press the start button tells you a lot. Slow cranking, a single click, or a normal crank that never catches each point to different problems.
causes: Dim lights, slow cranking or rapid clicking usually mean the battery is weak. Batteries wear with age, and short trips or leaving something on can drain them.
Poor contact at the terminals can act like a flat battery even when the battery is fine. Cleaning and tightening can help.
A single loud click, or a whirring sound with no engine turning, often points to the starter or its solenoid.
If a new or charged battery keeps going flat, the alternator may not be charging while you drive. A battery light on the dash is a clue.
If the engine turns over normally but never starts, the cause may be fuel delivery, a sensor or the ignition system rather than the battery.
A weak key fob battery or an immobiliser fault can stop some cars from starting even with a good battery.
tell: What you hear: nothing, a click, slow cranking, or normal cranking.
Whether the dashboard lights come on bright or dim.
Whether a jump start worked.
Age of the battery and whether the car sat unused or did short trips.
Whether a battery or other warning light came on while driving.
urgent: If the battery looks swollen, is leaking or smells of rotten eggs, do not jump start it. Call a workshop or breakdown service.
faqs: Can a jump start tell me if it is the battery?
Often yes. If it starts with a jump but dies again soon after, the alternator or a battery drain is more likely than the battery alone.
Do I need a new battery or a new starter?
It depends on the symptoms, so the workshop should test before replacing anything.

title: Gearbox or CVT Jerking: Causes | SG Car Workshop
h1: Gearbox or CVT jerking, shuddering or slipping
desc: Why an automatic gearbox or CVT jerks, shudders or hesitates, what to tell the workshop, and workshops customers mention for gearbox and fluid work.
lede: Jerking, shuddering or a delay when you pull away can come from the gearbox, but not always. Engine problems and worn mounts can feel the same, so a proper check matters before anyone talks about replacing a gearbox.
causes: The fluid cools and lubricates the gearbox. Old, burnt or low fluid is a common cause of rough shifting and shudder. Many makers list a fluid service interval in the manual.
A CVT uses a belt or chain and pulleys; a conventional automatic uses clutches. Wear here can cause shudder, slipping or a whining noise.
These control the fluid pressure that makes the gearbox shift. A fault can cause harsh or delayed shifts.
The gearbox computer relies on sensors. A fault can cause odd shifting, and a warning light may come on.
A misfiring engine or a worn engine or gearbox mount can feel like gearbox jerking. This is why the whole picture needs checking.
tell: When it happens: cold start, pulling away, a particular speed, or when braking.
Whether it jerks in Drive only or also in Reverse.
Any warning lights or fluid leaks under the car.
When the gearbox fluid was last changed.
Ask for a scan for fault codes and a fluid check before any major work.
urgent: If the gearbox slips badly, will not move the car, or you see a fluid leak or smell burning, avoid driving it and have it checked.
faqs: Does every jerk mean a gearbox rebuild?
No. Fluid, a sensor or an engine problem can cause similar symptoms. Ask for the cheaper checks first, such as a scan and a fluid inspection.
Should I change CVT fluid?
Follow the maker's guidance for your model and ask the workshop which fluid is specified. CVTs are often fussy about the fluid used.

title: Brake Squeal and Noise: Causes | SG Car Workshop
h1: Brake squeal, squeak or grinding
desc: Why brakes squeal, squeak or grind, which sounds can wait and which cannot, what to tell the workshop, and workshops customers mention for brake work.
lede: Brake noise is common and not always serious, but grinding is a warning. Knowing which sound you have helps the workshop find the cause quickly.
causes: Many pads have a small metal tab that squeals when the pad is nearly worn out. It is meant to warn you to have the pads changed.
Glazed or hard pads and discs
Hard braking or heat can leave a glossy surface that squeals. Some pads are simply noisier than others.
A light squeal that goes away after a few stops, especially after rain or in the morning, is often just moisture or dust. Missing shims or dry contact points can also cause squeaks.
Grooves or a lip on the disc can cause noise and reduce braking performance.
A caliper that does not release fully can cause noise, heat and uneven wear. The car may pull to one side.
tell: Is it a squeal, a squeak or a grinding sound?
Does it happen when braking, when you release, or all the time?
Front or rear, and one side or both.
How the pedal feels and whether the car pulls to one side.
When the pads were last changed.
urgent: A deep grinding sound, a soft or long brake pedal, or the car pulling hard to one side needs attention straight away. Do not keep driving on grinding brakes.
faqs: Why do my brakes squeal only in the morning?
Moisture on the discs overnight can cause a short squeal that clears after a few stops. If it stays, have the pads checked.
Can I just change the pads?
Often yes, but the discs, calipers and slide pins should be checked at the same time.

title: Engine Warning Light On: Causes | SG Car Workshop
h1: Engine warning light on
desc: What the engine or check-engine light can mean, which cases need action now, what to tell the workshop, and workshops customers mention for diagnosis.
lede: The engine warning light means the car has stored a fault. It can be minor, like a loose fuel cap, or something that needs attention soon. A scan reads the fault codes, but the code points to a system, not always to the broken part.
causes: A cap that is not sealed can trigger an emissions fault. It is one of the simplest causes.
Misfire from spark plugs or ignition coils
Worn plugs or a weak coil make the engine run roughly. A flashing light usually means a misfire that can damage the catalytic converter.
Airflow (MAF), oxygen and other sensors feed the engine computer. A dirty or failing sensor can set a warning, sometimes fixed by cleaning.
Carbon build-up in the throttle body or EGR
Deposits can cause rough idle and warnings. Cleaning the parts can solve it in some cases.
These often follow other faults, such as long-term misfires, and may show as a loss of power or poor fuel use.
A cracked hose lets in extra air and upsets the fuel mix, causing rough running and a warning light.
tell: Is the light steady or flashing, and what colour?
Any symptoms: rough idle, loss of power, higher fuel use, smoke or smells.
Whether it came on after refuelling.
If anyone has read the codes, the code numbers.
Ask the workshop to explain the code and what they check before replacing a part.
urgent: A flashing light, a sudden loss of power, or a red oil pressure or temperature warning means you should stop driving and have it checked. A red oil pressure light means stop the engine at once.
faqs: Can I keep driving with the light on?
A steady light with the car driving normally can usually wait a short while for a check. A flashing light or loss of power should not be ignored.
Will the workshop just clear the code?
Clearing a code does not fix the cause and the light will come back. Ask what they found and what they did.

title: Car Overheating: Causes and What To Do | SG Car Workshop
h1: Car overheating
desc: Why a car overheats, what to do when the temperature gauge rises, what to tell the workshop, and workshops customers mention for cooling work.
lede: An engine that runs too hot can be damaged quickly, so overheating is something to deal with straight away. The causes are usually found in the cooling system.
causes: A leaking hose, radiator, water pump or gasket lets coolant escape. If the level is low, the engine cannot shed its heat.
Radiator fan or fan motor not working
In traffic, the fan pulls air through the radiator. If it fails, the engine can overheat when slow or stopped.
The thermostat controls coolant flow. If it sticks shut, the engine heats up and the top radiator hose may feel very hot while the bottom stays cool.
Dirt or scale can restrict flow, and a weak radiator cap cannot hold the pressure the system needs.
If the pump stops circulating coolant, temperature rises. A leak or a noise from the pump area can be a clue.
A failing gasket can push combustion gases into the coolant or let coolant mix with oil. It is more serious and needs prompt attention.
tell: When it runs hot: in traffic, on the highway, or with the aircon on.
Whether the coolant level has dropped and if you see leaks or puddles.
Steam, a sweet smell, or white smoke.
Whether the heater blows hot or cold.
Any recent work on the cooling system.
urgent: If the temperature gauge enters the red or a warning shows, pull over safely and switch off. Do not open the radiator cap while the engine is hot. Do not keep driving, as it can cause expensive engine damage.
faqs: Can I top up with water?
In an emergency it may get you to a workshop, but the correct coolant mix protects the engine. Ask the workshop to check the level and find the leak.
Is overheating always the radiator?
No. The fan, thermostat, water pump or a leak can all cause it, which is why a pressure test and a fan check help.

title: BMW and Mercedes Servicing Guide | SG Car Workshop
h1: BMW and Mercedes-Benz servicing and repair
desc: What owners of BMW and Mercedes-Benz cars can ask an independent workshop, common maintenance topics, and workshops customers mention for these brands.
lede: BMW and Mercedes-Benz cars are well served by independent workshops, provided the workshop knows the model and has the right diagnostic equipment. These notes cover what to ask and what tends to need attention.
causes: Servicing follows the car's own service indicator
Many of these cars show service messages based on use. Ask the workshop what they plan to do and which parts of the schedule they are covering.
Use the oil and parts the car calls for
These engines are particular about oil. Ask which oil specification they use and that it matches what the maker approves for your engine.
Plastic cooling parts, hoses and water pumps on many continental cars wear with age and heat. A coolant leak or temperature warning should be checked early.
Rubber bushes and mounts wear over time and can cause knocks, vibration or a loose feel. An undercarriage inspection is worth asking for on older cars.
Oil leaks from gaskets and housings
A slow oil leak from a valve cover or filter housing gasket is a common finding on older engines. Ask them to find the source before replacing parts.
Many newer models need a scan tool for diagnosis, and some jobs, such as a battery change, may need the car's system to be told about it. Ask whether the workshop can do this.
tell: Model, year and engine, and the chassis or model code if you know it.
Service history and when it was last serviced.
Warning messages on the dashboard.
Whether you want genuine, OEM or other quality parts.
Ask whether the workshop works on your model regularly.
urgent: Do not ignore a red warning on the dashboard, a coolant or oil warning, or a loss of power. Stop safely and get it checked.
faqs: Is an independent workshop okay for a BMW or Mercedes?
Many owners use independent workshops after the warranty ends. Ask what experience the workshop has with your model and what tools they use.
Do I need genuine parts?
It is your choice. Ask the workshop what options exist and what they recommend for each job.

title: Toyota Servicing and Repair Guide | SG Car Workshop
h1: Toyota servicing and repair
desc: What Toyota owners can ask a workshop, maintenance topics for common models including hybrids, and workshops customers mention for Toyota cars.
lede: Toyotas are common on Singapore roads, so most workshops see them often. These notes help you ask the right questions, especially if you drive a hybrid.
causes: Check the owner's manual or service booklet for the oil, filter and fluid intervals for your model, and ask the workshop to follow them.
Hybrid models need a hybrid-aware workshop
Hybrids have a high-voltage battery and system. Ask whether the workshop works on hybrids before booking anything beyond basic servicing.
Bushes, links and shock absorbers wear with distance. A noise over bumps is a reason to ask for an undercarriage inspection.
Weak aircon or a rising temperature gauge should be checked early, as small faults grow.
Some automatics and CVTs benefit from fluid changes at the interval the maker states. Ask which fluid is specified.
tell: Model, year and whether it is petrol or hybrid.
Mileage and service history.
Symptoms: noises, warning lights, vibration, smells.
What you want done, so you can compare what is included.
urgent: A red warning light, overheating or a loss of braking performance should be checked before you drive further.
faqs: Can any workshop service a hybrid Toyota?
Basic servicing is similar, but work involving the hybrid system needs the right training and tools. Ask the workshop directly.
How do I know what service my Toyota needs?
The owner's manual has the schedule. A good workshop will explain what each item is for and what can wait.

title: Honda Servicing and Repair Guide | SG Car Workshop
h1: Honda servicing and repair
desc: What Honda owners can ask a workshop, maintenance topics for common models, and workshops customers mention for Honda cars.
lede: Honda cars are widely used in Singapore. These notes cover what to ask the workshop and the maintenance topics that matter for many Honda models.
causes: Check the owner's manual for the oil, filter and fluid intervals for your model. Ask the workshop to quote against that schedule.
Many Honda models use a CVT, and these are usually specific about the fluid. Ask which fluid the workshop uses and why.
Keep the oil level and change interval in check. A slow oil leak from a gasket is worth finding early.
If the aircon is weak or noisy, have it checked for leaks and compressor health rather than only topping up.
Ask for an inspection of bushes, links and brakes at servicing, especially on cars with higher mileage.
Newer and hybrid models have more electronics. Ask whether the workshop has the diagnostic tools for your model.
tell: Model, year and engine or hybrid type.
Mileage and service history.
Symptoms: noises, shuddering, warning lights, smells.
Whether you want the work done to the maker's schedule or only fix the fault.
urgent: A red warning light, overheating or a drop in braking performance should be checked before you drive further.
faqs: Does my Honda need special fluid?
Many Honda transmissions are specific about fluid. Check the manual and ask the workshop which fluid they use.
Can an independent workshop service my Honda?
Yes, many owners use independent workshops. Ask about their experience with your model.

title: Tesla Servicing and Repair Guide | SG Car Workshop
h1: Tesla servicing and repair
desc: What Tesla owners in Singapore can ask an independent workshop, what to tell it, cautions on high-voltage work and body parts, and listings that name Tesla.
lede: A Tesla has no engine oil to change, but its tyres, brakes, suspension, aircon and bodywork still need looking after. These notes cover what to ask a workshop, what to tell it, and the cautions that come with an electric car.
causes: Ask which jobs the workshop does on Teslas
Many jobs, such as tyres, brakes, suspension arms and wheel alignment, are ordinary mechanical work. Ask the workshop which jobs it does on Teslas and which it sends elsewhere.
The main battery and its orange cables carry high voltage. Only staff trained on electric cars, with the right tools and safety steps, should work on them. Ask before you book.
Electric cars are heavy and deliver power at once, so tyres and suspension parts such as control arm bushes can wear. A knock over humps or uneven tyre wear is worth checking.
Regenerative braking means the pads are used less, but discs and calipers can still rust or stick when they are used lightly. Ask for a brake check at each visit.
The aircon compressor is electric and may need a specific oil. Ask whether the workshop handles aircon on electric cars before you book a gas top-up.
Body parts must match your exact version
Panels, sensors and camera mounts can differ between model years and versions. Share the model, year and a photo of the part so fitment is checked before anything is ordered.
Some faults are fixed by a software update, and some work can affect the maker's warranty. Check your warranty terms and any open recalls with the maker before you choose where to go.
tell: Model, year and version, for example Model 3 or Model Y and the year.
Mileage, and any warning message on the screen, with a photo.
Symptoms: noises, vibration, pulling, aircon not cold.
Whether the car is still under the maker's warranty.
For parts, a photo of the part and the car details so fitment can be checked.
urgent: A battery or high-voltage warning, a burning smell, smoke, or a car that will not go into drive should be checked before you drive further. Never open or work on the high-voltage battery or orange cables yourself.
few_note: Only a few listed workshops name Tesla so far. If none is near you, ask a workshop directly about its experience with your model.
faqs: Can an independent workshop service a Tesla?
Many jobs, such as tyres, brakes, suspension and aircon, are ordinary mechanical work. Ask the workshop about its experience with Teslas and what it does not handle.
Does a Tesla need regular servicing?
There is no engine oil to change, but tyres, brakes, suspension, the cabin filter and fluids still need checks. The maker's maintenance advice for your model says what and when.
What should I check before buying a body part?
Check that it matches your model, year and version, and ask the seller to confirm fitment from photos before you pay.

title: BYD Servicing and Repair Guide | SG Car Workshop
h1: BYD servicing and repair
desc: What BYD owners in Singapore can ask a workshop, what to tell it, cautions on high-voltage work and body parts, and listings that name BYD.
lede: BYD cars such as the Atto 3, Dolphin and Seal are often seen on Singapore roads. They still need tyres, brakes, suspension, aircon and bodywork looked after. These notes cover what to ask, what to tell the workshop, and the cautions for an electric car.
causes: Know whether your BYD is fully electric or a plug-in hybrid
Some BYD models are fully electric and some are plug-in hybrids with a petrol engine too. A plug-in hybrid also needs engine oil and engine servicing, so tell the workshop which one you drive.
The main battery and its orange cables carry high voltage. Only staff trained on electric cars, with the right tools and safety steps, should work on them. Ask before you book.
Electric cars are heavy, so tyres and suspension parts can wear. A knock over humps, a pull to one side or uneven tyre wear is worth checking.
Regenerative braking means the pads are used less, but discs and calipers can still rust or stick. Ask for a brake check at each visit.
The aircon compressor is electric and may need a specific oil. Ask whether the workshop handles aircon on electric cars.
Parts for newer models and versions may be less widely stocked. Share the exact model, year and a photo of the part so fitment is checked before anything is ordered.
Some work can affect the maker's warranty, including the battery warranty. Check your warranty terms and any open recalls with the dealer before you choose where to go.
tell: Model, year and whether it is fully electric or a plug-in hybrid.
Mileage, and any warning message on the screen, with a photo.
Symptoms: noises, vibration, pulling, aircon not cold.
Whether the car is still under the maker's warranty.
For parts, a photo of the part and the car details so fitment can be checked.
urgent: A battery or high-voltage warning, a burning smell, smoke, or a car that will not go into drive should be checked before you drive further. Never open or work on the high-voltage battery or orange cables yourself.
few_note: Only a few listed workshops name BYD so far. If none is near you, ask a workshop directly about its experience with your model.
faqs: Can an independent workshop service a BYD?
Many jobs, such as tyres, brakes, suspension and aircon, are ordinary mechanical work. Ask the workshop about its experience with BYD cars and what it does not handle.
Does an electric BYD need servicing?
A fully electric BYD has no engine oil to change, but tyres, brakes, suspension, the cabin filter and fluids still need checks. A plug-in hybrid also needs engine servicing.
What should I check before buying a body part?
Check that it matches your model, year and version, and ask the seller to confirm fitment from photos before you pay.

title: How to Choose a Car Workshop in Singapore | SG Car Workshop
h1: How to choose a car workshop or car repair workshop in Singapore
desc: A plain guide for drivers: how to pick a car workshop or car repair workshop in Singapore, what to ask before you book, and how to compare quotes.
lede: Most drivers look for a car workshop only when something goes wrong, so it helps to know what to look for before you need one. These are simple checks that work for servicing, repairs and accident work.
heading: What to look for
tell_h: What to ask before you book
urgent_h: Walk away or get a second opinion if:
causes: Work that matches your problem and your car
Some workshops do mostly servicing, others focus on gearbox, aircon, bodywork or certain makes. Check the services and car makes on the workshop page, and ask if they often work on your model.
A good habit is to ask for a written quote that lists parts and labour separately before any work starts, and to ask the workshop to call you before doing anything extra.
You should come away knowing what is wrong, why a part needs changing and what can wait. Ask to see the old parts that were replaced.
Ask whether they will fit original, OEM or aftermarket parts, and what the difference means for your car. Let them explain the options.
Ask whether the repair or parts come with a warranty, how long it lasts and what it covers. Keep the invoice.
Easy to reach and easy to get to
A workshop you can WhatsApp for updates, with opening hours that suit you and a location near home or work, makes follow-up visits simpler.
tell: Your car make, model, year and mileage.
What you have noticed and when it started.
Ask for a written quote before work starts.
Ask them to call you before any extra work.
Ask what warranty comes with the parts and labour.
Ask how long the job usually takes and whether you need to leave the car.
urgent: the quote keeps changing without a clear reason, you are pushed to decide on the spot, or the workshop will not explain what it found. Getting a second opinion on a big repair is normal.
faqs: Is a car workshop the same as a car repair workshop?
People use both words for the same thing: a place that services and repairs cars. Some focus on certain jobs, such as bodywork or gearbox, so check what each one lists.
Do I have to go back to the dealer for servicing?
Many owners use independent workshops after the warranty period. If your car is still under the maker's warranty, check its terms first, and keep every service record.
How many quotes should I get?
For a big repair, two or three quotes for the same job help you see what is fair. Make sure each quote covers the same parts and work.

title: Car Servicing Cost in Singapore: What Decides It
h1: How much does car servicing cost in Singapore?
desc: What decides the price of car servicing in Singapore, what a service usually includes, and how to get a clear quote for your car.
lede: There is no single price for a car service. What you pay depends on your car, the kind of service and the parts and oil used. We do not list prices: the only reliable figure is a quote from the workshop for your car.
heading: What decides the price
tell_h: How to get a clear quote
causes: Your car make, model and engine
Bigger engines, continental cars and hybrids often need more oil, specific fluids or special tools, which changes the cost.
A minor service is usually an oil and filter change with basic checks. A major service at a set mileage can add spark plugs, air and cabin filters, brake fluid, coolant or gearbox fluid.
Fully synthetic oil and oil approved by your car's maker cost more than basic oil. Your owner's manual lists the grade your engine needs.
The same filter or spark plug can come from different makers at different prices. Ask which one the quote uses.
Extra work found during the service
Worn brake pads, tyres or a weak battery may be found during the check. These are separate from the service itself, so ask for them to be quoted on their own.
tell: Your car make, model, year, engine and mileage.
Which service your manual says is due at this mileage.
Ask what the service includes, item by item.
Ask which oil grade and which parts the quote uses.
Ask them to call you before doing any extra work.
Ask for the price for your car: ask the workshop, as prices change.
urgent: a service price looks very different from another quote for the same items, or a long list of extra work is added without photos or an explanation.
faqs: How often should I service my car?

Follow the service interval in your owner's manual, which is set by distance or time, whichever comes first. Short trips and stop-start traffic can count as harder use, so ask the workshop what suits how you drive.
Why do two quotes for a service differ?
They may use different oil, different parts or include different checks. Ask each workshop for a list of what is included so you compare the same thing.
Can you tell me the price?
We do not publish prices because they depend on your car and change over time. WhatsApp the workshop with your car model and mileage and ask for a quote.

title: Car Dent Repair Near Me: What to Know | SG Car Workshop
h1: Car dent repair: what to know before you go
desc: Car dent and scratch repair in plain words: paintless dent repair, panel beating and respray, insurance claims, and workshops customers mention for dent work.
lede: A dent can often be fixed without repainting, but it depends on how deep it is and whether the paint is broken. Here is what the usual options mean, so you know what to ask.
heading: The usual ways to fix a dent
causes: For small, smooth dents where the paint is not cracked, a technician can push the metal back from behind or pull it out from the front. The original paint stays.
Deeper dents, creases or dents with broken paint are reshaped, filled and smoothed, then painted to match the rest of the car.
A badly damaged bumper, fender or door may be cheaper or better to replace than to repair. Ask the workshop to explain why.
Scratches on top of the dent
Light scratches may polish out. Scratches through the clear coat or paint need touch-up or a respray of that panel.
After a knock, sensors, brackets or lights behind the bumper can be damaged too. Ask for a check behind the panel.
tell: Where the dent is and how big it is, with a clear photo.
Whether the paint is cracked or scratched.
Your car make, model and colour.
Whether it is an insurance claim or you are paying yourself.
Ask how they will match the paint colour, if painting is needed.
Ask how long the car needs to stay.
urgent: a light, sensor or door no longer works after the knock, a panel is loose, or there are sharp edges. Get it checked before driving far.
faqs: Can I get a quote from a photo?
Many workshops will give a rough idea from a WhatsApp photo, but the final quote usually needs them to see the car.
Should I claim insurance for a small dent?
It depends on your policy, excess and no-claim discount. Check your policy and ask your insurer before you decide, and check how soon you must report an accident to them.
Does paintless dent repair work on every dent?
No. It suits small, smooth dents with unbroken paint. Sharp creases, edges and damaged paint usually need panel work.

title: Car Spray Painting in Singapore | SG Car Workshop
h1: Car spray painting: touch-up, panel respray or full respray
desc: A plain guide to car spray painting in Singapore: touch-up, single panel or full respray, colour matching, and workshops customers mention for spray work.
lede: Spray painting covers anything from one scratched panel to a whole new colour. Knowing which one you need helps you ask the right questions and compare workshops fairly.
heading: The usual kinds of spray work
causes: Small chips and light scratches can be touched up on the spot. It is quick but may still show up close.
One panel, such as a bumper or door, is prepared and painted to match. Good colour matching and blending into the next panel make it hard to see.
The whole car is painted, either in the same colour or a new one. It takes longer because panels and trims are removed and the surface is prepared.
If you change your car's colour, check the current Land Transport Authority (LTA) rules on updating your vehicle's colour records before you go ahead.
Many spray shops also paint rims, mirrors, grilles and trims. Ask what finish they use, such as gloss or matte.
tell: Which panels need painting, with photos.
Your car's colour name or paint code (often on a sticker in the door frame).
Whether you want the same colour or a new one.
Ask how they match the colour and whether they blend into the next panel.
Ask how long the car needs to stay and whether the paint has a warranty.
urgent: rust is coming through the paint or a panel is damaged underneath. The cause needs fixing first, or the new paint will not last.
faqs: How long does a respray take?
A small touch-up can be quick, while a panel or full respray takes longer because of preparation and drying. Ask the workshop for its usual time for your job.
Will a respray match my original paint?
Good workshops match the colour using the paint code and test it against the car. Ask to see the result in daylight before you collect the car.
Can I change my car colour in Singapore?
It is possible, but check the current LTA rules on recording a colour change before the work starts.

title: Car Dashboard Warning Lights Explained | SG Car Workshop
h1: Car dashboard warning lights: what they mean and what to do
desc: What the common car dashboard warning lights mean in plain words, which ones mean stop now, and what to tell the workshop.
lede: Dashboard lights follow a simple colour code on most cars. Red usually means stop safely and check, amber or yellow means get it checked soon, and green or blue just shows something is switched on. Your owner's manual has the exact meaning for your car.
heading: Common warning lights
urgent_h: Stop safely and call for help if:
causes: The engine may not be getting enough oil. Stop as soon as it is safe and switch off the engine. Driving on can damage the engine.
The engine is getting too hot. Stop safely, switch off and let it cool. Do not open the radiator cap while it is hot.
The battery is not being charged while you drive, often an alternator or belt problem. The car may run until the battery is flat.
It can mean the handbrake is on, brake fluid is low or there is a brake fault. If it stays on with the handbrake off, get it checked before driving on.
An engine or emissions fault has been stored. A steady light means get it checked soon; a flashing light means a more serious fault, so reduce speed and get it checked quickly.
ABS, airbag and tyre pressure lights
These show a fault in the anti-lock brakes, the airbag system or low tyre pressure. The car may drive normally, but safety systems may not work as they should.
tell: Which light came on, its colour, and whether it is steady or flashing.
When it came on: at start-up, while driving, or after a bump or heavy rain.
Any noises, smells, smoke or change in how the car drives.
Ask the workshop to read the fault codes with a diagnostic scanner and explain them.
urgent: a red oil, temperature or brake light comes on, the check engine light is flashing, or you see smoke or smell burning.
faqs: Can I keep driving with the check engine light on?
If it is steady and the car drives normally, you can usually drive carefully to a workshop soon. If it flashes or the car feels wrong, stop and get help.
Will the light go off by itself?
Some faults clear after the cause is fixed, such as a loose fuel cap. The workshop can read the stored code to tell you what it was.
Is this the same as the engine warning light guide?
This guide covers all the common lights. For the check engine light in more detail, see the engine warning light guide.

title: Car Battery Dead: What to Do Next | SG Car Workshop
h1: Car battery dead: jump start, charge or replace?
desc: What to do when your car battery is dead in Singapore: safe jump starting, signs the battery needs replacing, and workshops customers mention for battery work.
lede: A flat battery is one of the most common reasons a car will not start. Sometimes a jump start is enough, sometimes the battery is worn out, and sometimes the battery is fine but is not being charged.
heading: What usually causes it
tell_h: What to tell the workshop or battery service
causes: Headlights, cabin lights or a dashcam left running can drain the battery overnight. A jump start and a good drive usually recharges it.
Car batteries wear out with age and heat. If it is a few years old and keeps going weak, a battery test will show whether it needs replacing.
Short, slow trips may not give the alternator enough time to recharge the battery, especially with the aircon and lights on.
If a new or charged battery goes flat again, the alternator or a drive belt may not be charging it. A battery light on the dashboard is a clue.
A faulty accessory or wiring can drain the battery while the car is parked. A workshop can test for it.
tell: What happens when you start: slow cranking, clicking, or nothing at all.
How old the battery is, if you know.
Whether it has happened before and how often.
Where the car is, if you need someone to come to you.
Ask them to test the battery and the charging system, not only replace the battery.
urgent: you smell rotten eggs, see the battery swelling or leaking, or see smoke. Do not try to jump start it; keep away and call for help.
faqs: Is it safe to jump start my car myself?
It can be, if you follow the order in your owner's manual, use proper cables and connect to the right points. Some cars, including many hybrids, have their own rules, so check the manual first.
How do I know if the battery needs replacing?
Slow starts, dim lights and a battery that keeps going flat are common signs. A workshop or battery service can test it in a few minutes.
Can someone come to my car?
Some battery services and workshops can come to you. Check the workshop page or ask by WhatsApp.

title: What to Check Before a Car Workshop Visit | SG Car Workshop
h1: What to check before you take your car to a workshop
desc: A simple checklist for drivers before a car workshop visit: what to note down, what to bring, what to ask, and what to check when you collect the car.
lede: A few minutes of preparation makes a workshop visit faster and helps you get a clear answer and a fair quote. Use this list before you go and when you collect the car.
heading: Before you go
tell_h: When you drop off and collect the car
urgent_h: Do not drive to the workshop if:
causes: Write down what you notice, when it happens and when it started. A short video of a noise or a photo of a warning light helps a lot.
Have your car make, model, year and mileage ready, and the date of the last service.
Bring your service booklet or past invoices, and any warranty papers for earlier repairs.
WhatsApp the workshop with your car details and the problem, and ask when they can look at it and how long it may take.
Take out valuables and anything you need. Note the fuel level and mileage when you hand over the car.
tell: Ask for a written quote before any work starts.
Ask them to call you before any extra work.
Ask for the old parts back or to see them.
When you collect the car, check the invoice against the quote.
Take a short test drive to check the problem is fixed.
Keep the invoice for warranty and resale.
urgent: a red warning light is on, the car is overheating, the brakes feel wrong or fluid is leaking. Ask the workshop about towing instead.
faqs: Do I need an appointment?
Many workshops take walk-ins, but booking ahead by WhatsApp saves waiting time. Check the opening hours on the workshop page.
Should I wait at the workshop?
For a quick job you may be able to wait. For diagnosis or bigger repairs, ask how long it usually takes and whether you need to leave the car.
What if the problem comes back?
Contact the workshop with your invoice. Many workshops give a warranty on their work, so ask about it when you collect the car.

title: Tyre Shop Open on Sunday in Singapore | SG Car Workshop
h1: Tyre shop open on Sunday in Singapore: what to check
desc: Flat tyre on a Sunday in Singapore? What to check before you drive, what to ask a tyre shop, and listed tyre shops whose Google hours show Sunday open.
lede: Many workshops in Singapore close on Sunday, so a flat or damaged tyre at the weekend can feel stuck. Some tyre shops do open on Sunday. A few checks before you drive over save a wasted trip and help you get the right tyre fitted.
heading: Before you drive over
tell_h: What to ask the tyre shop
urgent_h: Do not drive on the tyre if:
causes: Check how bad the damage is
A nail in the tread can often be repaired. A cut or bulge in the sidewall, or a tyre that has been driven flat, usually needs a new tyre. Take a clear photo of the damage.
The size is printed on the sidewall, for example 195/65 R15 91H. Send it to the shop so it can check stock before you come.
Fit the spare or use the repair kit if you can
If the car has a spare wheel, fitting it is usually the safest way to reach the shop. Some cars only carry a sealant kit; follow the instructions in the owner's manual.
Check the Sunday hours on the day
Sunday hours can change, and some shops close on certain public holidays. Message the shop first, even when its Google Maps hours show it open.
Decide whether you want to replace one tyre or a pair on the same axle, and whether you prefer a particular brand.
tell: Your tyre size and car model, with a photo of the damage.
Whether the tyre can be repaired or needs replacing.
Which tyre brands and sizes are in stock today.
Whether wheel balancing and new valves are included.
Whether the other tyre on the same axle should be replaced too.
How long the job takes, so you know whether to wait.
urgent: the sidewall is cut or bulging, the tyre is flat or nearly flat, or the car pulls hard or shakes. Fit the spare or call for roadside help instead.
faqs: Can a punctured tyre be repaired?
Often, if the hole is small and in the tread area. Damage in the sidewall or a tyre driven while flat usually means replacing it. Only an inspection can confirm it.
Do I need wheel balancing after a new tyre?
Yes, a wheel is normally balanced after a new tyre is fitted, so the car does not vibrate. Ask if it is included.
Should I replace tyres in pairs?
Many drivers replace both tyres on the same axle so they wear and grip evenly. Ask the shop about the tread left on the other tyre.
How do I know a shop is open on Sunday?
Check its Google Maps hours, then message it before you drive over. Hours can change on public holidays.

title: Car Burning Smell: Causes and What To Do | SG Car Workshop
h1: Burning smell from your car: what it can mean
desc: What a burning smell from your car can mean, from rubber and oil to clutch, plastic or sweet coolant, when to stop driving and what to tell the workshop.
lede: A burning smell usually comes from one of five things: rubber from a tyre or a dragging brake, hot oil, a slipping clutch, an electrical fault, or leaking coolant. The kind of smell and when you notice it help a workshop find the cause. If there is smoke, a warning light or the temperature gauge is rising, stop somewhere safe and switch off.
heading: What the smell can mean
urgent_h: Stop driving when it is safe if:
causes: Often a brake that is dragging or very hot, for example after a long downhill or with the handbrake left on, or a tyre rubbing on a part. A slipping drive belt can smell similar.
Burning oil or a sharp, acrid smell

Oil dripping onto the hot engine or exhaust smells sharp, sometimes with light smoke from under the bonnet. Spilled oil after an oil change can smell for a short while, but a smell that keeps coming back points to a leak.
A slipping clutch smells like burnt paper, often after slow stop-start driving or a hill start in a manual car. In an automatic or CVT, overheated gearbox fluid can also smell burnt.

A smell of hot plastic or wiring can come from a wiring fault, a fuse, the blower motor or an added accessory. Electrical faults can get worse, so have it checked soon by a workshop that does electrical diagnosis.
A sweet smell, sometimes with steam or a damp floor mat, usually means coolant is leaking. Keep an eye on the temperature gauge.
tell: What the smell is like: rubber, oil, burnt paper, plastic or sweet.
When it happens: after a long drive, when braking, on hills, in traffic, or with the aircon on.
Where it seems to come from: a wheel, under the bonnet, or inside through the vents.
Any smoke, warning lights or a rising temperature gauge.
Any recent work, such as an oil change, new brakes or a new accessory.
urgent: you see smoke, smell burning plastic or wires, a red warning light comes on, or the temperature gauge moves towards hot. Pull over, switch off and get help. If you see flames, get everyone out and away from the car and call 995. A faint smell that fades soon after a long drive is less urgent, but still have it checked.
faqs: Is a burning smell after a long drive normal?
A faint smell of hot brakes after a long downhill, or of spilled oil just after an oil change, can fade on its own. A smell that keeps coming back, gets stronger or comes with smoke needs checking.
Can I keep driving with a burning smell?
If there is no smoke, no warning light and the temperature gauge is normal, drive gently to a workshop. If any of those show, stop safely and switch off first.
Why does my car smell burnt when the aircon is on?
Dust on a heater or blower, a blower motor fault, or a smell drawn in from outside are possible. A smell of burning plastic from the vents should be checked soon.
What does a workshop check first?
Usually the brakes and tyres, oil leaks around the engine and exhaust, the clutch or gearbox fluid, the coolant level and the wiring. Telling them the kind of smell and when it happens saves time.

title: Car Vibrating or Steering Wheel Shaking? | SG Car Workshop
h1: Car vibrating or steering wheel shaking: what it can mean
desc: Why a car vibrates or the steering wheel shakes at speed, when braking or when idling, which checks a workshop does first and when to stop driving.
lede: A shake you feel through the steering wheel, seat or pedal usually comes from the wheels and tyres, the brakes, worn steering or suspension parts, or the engine and its mounts. When it happens is the most useful clue: only at certain speeds, only when braking, or while standing still. If the shake is sudden and strong, stop somewhere safe and check the tyres before driving on.
heading: What the vibration can mean
urgent_h: Stop driving when it is safe if:
causes: Shake at certain speeds, often on the expressway

A wheel that is out of balance usually shakes the steering wheel in one speed range, then smooths out above it. A tyre with a bulge, uneven wear or a lost balance weight, or a bent rim after hitting a kerb or pothole, can feel the same.
Shake or pulsing when you brake
A steering wheel that shakes, or a brake pedal that pulses, mainly when you brake from speed often points to uneven brake discs. Worn pads or a sticking caliper can add noise or a pull to one side.
Car pulls to one side or the steering feels loose
Wheel alignment that is out, worn steering joints or tired suspension parts can make the car wander, pull or wobble over bumps. Tyres wearing on one edge are a common sign.
Vibration while idling or at a red light

If the whole car shakes while standing still, the engine may be running unevenly, for example from a misfire, or a worn engine mount may be letting normal engine movement through. A flashing engine light with shaking needs attention soon.
Shudder when pulling away or changing gear

A judder as the car moves off, or a shudder during gear changes, can come from the clutch, the gearbox or a worn drive shaft joint. A clicking sound on full lock in a car park is a common sign of a worn joint.
tell: When it shakes: at a certain speed, when braking, when idling, when pulling away or when turning.
Where you feel it: steering wheel, seat, brake pedal or the whole car.
Whether it started after hitting a kerb or pothole, a tyre change or a puncture repair.
Any warning lights, noises such as clicking or knocking, or the car pulling to one side.
When the tyres were last balanced, rotated or aligned, if you know.
urgent: the shake starts suddenly and is strong, a tyre looks flat or has a bulge, the steering feels loose, the engine light flashes, or you hear grinding when braking. Pull over somewhere safe, switch on the hazard lights and check the tyres. If you are unsure, do not drive on: call for roadside help.
faqs: Why does my steering wheel shake only at higher speeds?
A wheel out of balance is the most common reason. It often shows in one speed range and fades above it. A tyre shop can check the balance and look for tyre damage or a bent rim.
Is wheel balancing the same as wheel alignment?

No. Balancing evens out the weight around each wheel so it spins smoothly. Alignment sets the angle of the wheels so the car drives straight. A shake usually points to balance; a pull or uneven tyre wear usually points to alignment.
Why does the steering wheel shake when I brake?
Often the brake discs have worn unevenly. A workshop will check the discs and pads, and the calipers for sticking. Have it looked at soon, as braking is a safety system.
Can I keep driving with a vibration?
A mild shake that has been the same for a while can usually wait for a booked check, but drive gently. A sudden or strong shake, a damaged tyre or loose steering means stop safely first.
What does a workshop check first?
Usually the tyres, wheel balance and rims, then the brakes, steering and suspension joints, and engine mounts or misfires if it shakes when idling. Saying when the shake happens saves time.
